text: Talking about it with my parents and later with my roommate. My mum's calm was the main thing. Time.
Ich habe mit Freundinnen darüber gesprochen. Ich gehe inzwischen wieder in Bars, aber nicht mehr in Clubs.

I didn't tell anyone except my husband and sister for a long time because I was so ashamed. When my anxiety about the kids got really bad, I finally told my GP, who referred me to a therapist. The therapist helped me separate the drug-induced images from reality and work on the guilt. We did some exposure work, like leaving the kids with my sister for an afternoon, then a night. That helped. I've also done a mindfulness course. Self-compassion work has been the most important, but it's still hard.

Die Studie bot mehrere Integrationsgespräche an, die mir sehr geholfen haben. Die Begleiterin, die meine Hand gehalten hat, hat mit mir über diesen Moment gesprochen. Danach habe ich eine reguläre Psychotherapie fortgesetzt. Ich nehme weiterhin Antidepressiva. Die Depression ist nicht weg, aber etwas leichter.

I was treated by a psychiatrist for the psychotic episode, with a low dose of an antipsychotic for about three months. After that I started CBT for psychosis, which helped me deal with the doubts about my partner and the fear of going crazy. Couples therapy was important for us. I've also learned to recognise when I'm tired or stressed and the doubts might creep in, and I take that as a sign to rest. I haven't taken any psychedelics since and I won't. Reading other people's stories of 'Capgras-like' experiences on psychedelics helped me feel less alone, but I had to stop reading because some of them made me more scared.

Ich habe mit einer Psychologin über die Schuldgefühle gesprochen, das hat mir geholfen zu verstehen, dass ich in dem Moment nicht handlungsfähig war. Später habe ich der Organisation, über die wir die Reise gebucht hatten, einen Bericht geschickt. Sie haben nicht reagiert. Ich mache viel Sport, um mich in meinem Körper wieder sicher zu fühlen. Die Albträume sind seltener geworden.
Talked to some friends. Read a bit about DMT. Time mostly.

In Europe I got access to a psychologist through a refugee support organisation. She works with an interpreter, which is difficult because I don't want to talk about being gay in front of someone from my region. Later I found a therapist who speaks English, which is better. We are doing trauma therapy, NET (narrative exposure therapy). It is very hard but I feel it is helping a little.

A doctor prescribed me mirtazapine for sleep and depression. It helps me sleep, but I gain weight.

An LGBTQ refugee group has been the most helpful. There I can be myself and talk with people who understand. We meet every week.

I try to go running and I have started to learn the language, which gives me some structure.

Not helpful: the asylum interviews, where I had to describe everything again and again to officials who did not seem to believe me. After every interview I had nightmares for a week.

I am still struggling a lot. Some days are okay, many are not.
